label: Undergraduate studies at Cal Tech
description: Studied chemistry with Professors Swift, Yost, Pauling, and Lucas.

sources.quote: As an undergraduate in 1936-40 at Cal Tech, I was especially stimulated in many directions by Professors Ernest Swift, Don Yost, Linus Pauling and by Howard Lucas with whom I did undergraduate organic chemical research.

label: Ph.D. work at UC Berkeley
description: Conducted Ph.D. work on the kinetics of enolization of ketones under Axel Olson.

sources.quote: As a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, I was pointed in additional directions by Professors Ermon Eastman, Wendell Latimer, Joel Hildebrand, Gilbert Lewis, Gerhard Rollefson, and Axel Olson with whom I did my Ph.D. work on the kinetics of enolization of ketones.

label: Joined Manhattan Project
description: Approached by Wendell Latimer to predict properties of plutonium metal.

sources.quote: after completion of my thesis, I was approached by Wendell Latimer in December 1942 to join the Manhattan Project.

label: Sent CeS crucibles to Los Alamos
description: Delivered 564 cerium sulfide crucibles for plutonium metallurgy.

sources.quote: we had sent 564 crucibles to Los Alamos by the end of 1944.

label: Niels Engel sabbatical at Berkeley
description: Engel introduced Brewer to his theory of metallic bonding.

sources.quote: In the late forties, the Danish scientist Niels Engel spent a sabbatical at Berkeley and introduced me to his theory of metallic bonding

label: Presentation at Paul Beck's meeting
description: Presented chemist's view of metallic bonding and Engel's theory.

sources.quote: In 1962, Professor Paul Beck of the University of Illinois asked me if J would give a presentation of the chemist's view of metallic bonding at a meeting at which similar presentations would be made by metallurgists and physicists.

label: Teaching undergraduate inorganic laboratory
description: Taught course where students undertook minor research projects on intermetallics.

sources.quote: in 1966, I was teaching an undergraduate inorganic laboratory course in which the students undertook minor research projects.

label: Received letter from Paul Wengert
description: Wengert requested to do Ph.D. research with Brewer despite being a metallurgy student.

sources.quote: In 1969, I received a letter from Paul Wengert, an undergraduate student in metallurgy, who had read my papers and wanted to do Ph.D. research with me even though he was not a chemist.
